- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) and price shows no clear trend, model overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.15), model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.0% buffer for potential drop.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral, forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overbought trap.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overestimates momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
